## Definition

A (non-super) **vertex algebra** over $\mathbb C$ is a complex vector space $V$ equipped with a nonzero vector $\mathbf1\in V$, a linear operator $T:V\to V$, and a linear **state–field map**
$$Y(-,z):V\longrightarrow (\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V))^{\mathbb Z},\qquad a\longmapsto Y(a,z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}a_{(n)}z^{-n-1},$$
where the codomain denotes all endomorphism-valued coefficient families indexed by $\mathbb Z$.
satisfying the following axioms.

1. **Field and truncation.** For each $a,v\in V$, there is an integer $N(a,v)$ such that $a_{(n)}v=0$ for all $n\ge N(a,v)$. Thus $Y(a,z)v\in V((z))$ in the lower-bounded support sense of [[def-formal-laurent-series-and-residue]].

2. **Vacuum and creation.** $Y(\mathbf1,z)=\operatorname{id}_V$, $T\mathbf1=0$, and
   $$Y(a,z)\mathbf1=e^{zT}a:=\sum_{r\ge0}\frac{z^rT^r a}{r!}.$$
   This is a formal power series; no analytic convergence is asserted.

3. **Translation covariance.** For every $a\in V$,
   $$[T,Y(a,z)]=\partial_zY(a,z).$$

4. **Locality.** For every $a,b\in V$, some integer $N\ge0$ satisfies
   $$(z-w)^N[Y(a,z),Y(b,w)]=0.$$

The coefficient $a_{(n)}b$ is called the $n$th product of the states $a,b$. The mode and formal-distribution conventions in [[def-formal-distribution-on-a-vector-space]] are in force. The axioms are algebraic and do not impose a grading, conformal vector, simplicity, unitarity, or analytic OPE convergence.

## Remarks

The creation axiom is the strong form of the vacuum condition: it gives a formal power series in $z$ with coefficients in $V$ and constant coefficient $a$. Together with translation covariance and $T\mathbf1=0$, it fixes every coefficient of that vacuum series by the recursion $(r+1)[z^{r+1}]Y(a,z)\mathbf1=T([z^r]Y(a,z)\mathbf1)$.

## Definition

Let $V$ be a complex vector space. A **formal distribution** in variables $z,w$ with coefficients in a complex vector space $E$ is an arbitrary coefficient family
$$F(z,w)=\sum_{p,q\in\mathbb Z}F_{p,q}z^pw^q,\qquad F_{p,q}\in E.$$
No convergence or summability is assumed. Multiplication by a polynomial in $z,w$ is defined coefficientwise; each resulting coefficient is a finite sum. The residue $\operatorname{Res}_z F$ is the coefficient of $z^{-1}$, retaining the other variables and coefficients. For a one-variable series $f(z)=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}f_mz^m$, write $\operatorname{Res}_z f=f_{-1}$, in the same support convention as [[def-formal-laurent-series-and-residue]].

The **formal delta distribution** is
$$\delta(z,w)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}z^{-n-1}w^n.$$
For each integer $r$, the two binomial expansions of $(z-w)^r$ are
$$\iota_{z,w}(z-w)^r=\sum_{j\ge0}\binom rj(-1)^jz^{r-j}w^j,\qquad \iota_{w,z}(z-w)^r=\sum_{j\ge0}\binom rjz^j(-w)^{r-j},$$
where $\binom rj=r(r-1)\cdots(r-j+1)/j!$ and $\binom r0=1$. The first expansion is in nonnegative powers of $w$ and the second is in nonnegative powers of $z$; they are distinct when $r<0$.

A formal distribution $A(z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}A_nz^{-n-1}$ with $A_n\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ is a **field on $V$** if for every $v\in V$ there is an integer $N(v,A)$ such that $A_nv=0$ for all $n\ge N(v,A)$. Equivalently, $A(z)v\in V((z))$: its powers of $z$ are bounded below, as in [[def-formal-laurent-series-and-residue]], with coefficients in $V$. Define its modes by $A_{(n)}=A_n=\operatorname{Res}_z z^nA(z)$.

Two fields $A(z),B(w)$ are **mutually local** if some integer $N\ge0$ satisfies $(z-w)^N[A(z),B(w)]=0$ as a formal distribution, where $[A(z),B(w)]=A(z)B(w)-B(w)A(z)$. For any integer $n$, their **$n$th product field** is
$$A(z)_{(n)}B(z)=\operatorname{Res}_x\Bigl(\iota_{x,z}(x-z)^nA(x)B(z)-\iota_{z,x}(x-z)^nB(z)A(x)\Bigr).$$
These conventions use ordinary, ungraded vector spaces and ordinary commutators; no super sign is implicit.

## Remarks

- A formal distribution may have infinitely many positive and negative powers. A field has the additional vectorwise lower-truncation condition; the two notions are not interchangeable.
- The symbols $\iota_{z,w}$ and $\iota_{w,z}$ specify formal expansions only. They do not refer to analytic regions or convergence.

$k$-vector space $V$ is a unital $k$-linear algebra action on $V$; the two
items here define that interface and prove its equivalence with a $k$-bilinear
unital left $A$-module action. General module and tensor-product constructions
remain on [[tensor-products-of-modules]].

For a Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, the canonical map to
[[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]] turns a Lie representation into a
unital $U(\mathfrak g)$-module by
[[thm-lie-algebra-representations-are-equivalent-to-unital-modules-over-the-enveloping-algebra]].
Its tensor-product action is
$x(v\otimes w)=xv\otimes w+v\otimes xw$ by
[[prop-direct-sum-dual-hom-and-tensor-representations]], consistent with the
primitive coproduct on $U(\mathfrak g)$ in
[[rem-hopf-algebra-structure-on-the-enveloping-algebra]]. A Lie-algebra module
alone does not specify an integrated representation of a chosen global Lie
group.

The category of modules over a bialgebra becomes monoidal because its
coproduct defines the tensor action and its counit defines the unit object
([[def-monoidal-category]], [[def-hh-module-category-and-tensor-action]],
[[thm-hh-bialgebra-module-tensor-coherence]]). A monoidal category has
associators and unitors satisfying the pentagon and triangle; a braiding is
additional structure. A quasitriangular structure $R$ supplies a braiding on
bialgebra modules by
[[thm-hh-r-matrix-constructs-a-module-braiding]], and the braiding is symmetric
only in the triangular case described in
[[def-hh-braiding-and-triangular-structure]]. Here $R$ is an actual finite
algebraic tensor in $H\otimes H$; completed universal $R$-matrices require a
separate convergence and completion argument.

## Objective

This page constructs the untwisted Hall algebra of a small finitary abelian
category over an arbitrary commutative coefficient ring. With the fixed
convention that $[M]*[N]$ counts subobjects isomorphic to $N$ with quotient
isomorphic to $M$, its local proofs establish finite coefficients, finite
support, the zero-object unit, and associativity by counting two-step flags.
They use finite Hom sets and finite Yoneda $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ sets; they do
not assume finite-field linearity, enough projectives or injectives, or a
finite-subobject condition for every object.

A separate finite-field specialization develops the Jordan-quiver Hall
algebra. It proves the partition classification, Hall-polynomial structure
constants, and the generator-normalized isomorphism from its generic algebra
to the stable symmetric-function ring. The normalized partition basis is
identified with the monic Hall–Littlewood functions, and the inverse-
automorphism Green pairing is computed in power-sum coordinates by an
independent pair-of-flags count. The detailed calculations are on the
[[finitary-ringel-hall-algebras-examples|companion examples page]].

## Reading route and logical suppliers

The canonical plan declares both
[[algebraic-representation-and-tensor-symmetry-map]] and
[[cyclotomic-klr-algebras-and-highest-weight-categorification]] as page-level
reading prerequisites. These routes provide algebra and categorification
context. Neither is used as an item-level premise in the Hall counting proofs.
In particular, the published quiver-flag/KLR convolution theorem is a distinct
construction and does not establish Hall-product associativity.

## Normalization and scope

The coefficient $g^L_{M,N}$ is an integer count of subobject classes. Its
image in the coefficient ring is formed by repeated addition; no automorphism
cardinality is divided out. The square-root Euler twist, Green coproduct and
quantum-group comparison have additional hypotheses and belong to later
pages.

The Hall product $*$ is a multiplication on the Hall module. The Hall inner
product on symmetric functions is a separate bilinear form, defined by
[[def-hall-inner-product-on-symmetric-functions]]. The generic ring
isomorphism uses $\Phi_q(u_{(1^r)})=q^{-r(r-1)/2}e_r$. The local
[[thm-jordan-hall-pairing-and-hall-littlewood-basis]] proves
$\Phi_q(u_\lambda)=q^{-n(\lambda)}P_\lambda(x;q^{-1})$. The transported
Green form on degree $d$ is $q^{-d}$ times the standard Hall–Littlewood
form at parameter $q^{-1}$; its power-sum norms are
$z_\lambda\prod_i(q^{\lambda_i}-1)^{-1}$. These are distinct from the
ordinary Hall inner product. This Jordan pairing computation requires no
general Green coproduct theorem.

## Definition

Let $\mathcal A$ be a small finitary abelian category in the sense of
[[def-hall-finitary-abelian-category]], and let $R$ be a commutative ring
with unit. Define the free $R$-module
$$ H_{\mathcal A,R}:=\bigoplus_{[M]\in\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal A)}R[M], $$
where $[M]$ is a basis symbol for the isomorphism class of $M$. For objects $N,L$, let
$$\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal A}(N,L):=\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(N,L): f\text{ is monic}\}.$$
This is a finite set by the Hom condition in
[[def-hall-finitary-abelian-category]]. For $f,g$ in this set, write
$f\sim_N g$ when $g=f\circ u$ for an isomorphism $u:N\to N$; this is an
equivalence relation by [[def-isomorphism-groupoid-and-connected-category]].
The quotient set $\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal A}(N,L)/\sim_N$ represents
exactly the subobjects of $L$ isomorphic to $N$: each class gives the usual
subobject class from [[def-subobject-and-quotient-object]], and the mutual-
factorisation theorem says two such monomorphisms give the same subobject
exactly when they differ by such an isomorphism
([[thm-mutual-factorisation-defines-subobject-and-quotient-object-equivalence]]).
Every subobject class with domain isomorphic to $N$ is represented by composing
its monomorphism with an isomorphism from $N$, one class at a time. The
cokernel quotient is independent of that representative by
[[thm-the-quotient-is-independent-of-the-representing-monomorphism]] and
[[def-the-quotient-of-an-object-by-a-subobject]]. Define $g^L_{M,N}$ to be the
number of classes $[f]_{\sim_N}$ for which $\operatorname{coker}(f)\cong M$.
The finiteness lemma below also proves that the resulting product has finite
support. Extend the operation
$$ [M]*[N]:=\sum_{[L]\in\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal A)}g^L_{M,N}[L] $$
$R$-bilinearly, mapping each natural number coefficient to its multiple of
$1_R$. The order is fixed: the counted short exact sequence is
$$ 0\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow0. $$

This is the **untwisted Hall product**. It does not use an Euler form, a square
root of a field size, or division by automorphism cardinalities. The finite
coefficient and finite-support claims needed for the operation to define a
bilinear product are established in
[[lem-untwisted-hall-product-finiteness]].

## Statement

Let $k=\mathbb F_q$, and let $I_\lambda$ denote the nilpotent Jordan-quiver
representation indexed by a partition $\lambda$, as in
[[lem-jordan-quiver-isoclasses-are-partition-indexed]]. For partitions
$\mu,\nu,\lambda$, let $g^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(q)$ be the coefficient of
$[I_\lambda]$ in the untwisted product $[I_\mu]*[I_\nu]$. There are
polynomials $G^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(t)\in\mathbb Z[t]$, independent of the
finite field, with
$$ g^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(q)=G^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(q). $$
A coefficient is zero unless $|\lambda|=|\mu|+|\nu|$.

Define the **generic Jordan-quiver Hall algebra** by
$$ H_{\mathrm{gen}}:=\bigoplus_\lambda\mathbb Z[t]u_\lambda, \qquad u_\mu*u_\nu:=\sum_\lambda G^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(t)u_\lambda, $$
giving $u_\lambda$ degree $|\lambda|$ and $t$ degree $0$.
The size condition above makes this a graded algebra.
Then $H_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is a commutative associative unital algebra and a free
polynomial algebra over $\mathbb Z[t]$ on the classes
$u_{(1^r)}$, $r\ge1$. After extending scalars to
$\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$, the assignment
$$ \Phi_t(u_{(1^r)})=t^{-r(r-1)/2}e_r $$
for every $r\ge1$, and $\Phi_t(u_\varnothing)=1$, extends uniquely to a
graded algebra isomorphism
$$ H_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_{\mathbb Z[t]}\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}] \;\cong\; \Lambda\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}], $$
where $\Lambda$ is the stable graded ring of symmetric functions.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite field $k=\mathbb F_q$, its cardinality $q$, the
Jordan-quiver category $\mathcal J_k$, and an integer $r\ge0$ when a simple
direct-sum multiplicity is used.

[F1] The untwisted product coefficient counts subobjects $N$ with quotient
$M$, and its structure constants lie in the natural numbers before their
image in a coefficient ring ([[def-untwisted-hall-algebra]]).

[F2] The product is finite-support and associative, with zero-object unit
([[lem-untwisted-hall-product-finiteness]], [[thm-untwisted-hall-algebra-is-associative-and-unital]]).

[F3] The category is finitary over every finite field
([[lem-jordan-quiver-category-is-finitary]]).

[F4] Isomorphism classes are the partition-indexed objects $I_\lambda$,
and each is a direct sum of Jordan blocks ([[lem-jordan-quiver-isoclasses-are-partition-indexed]]).

[F5] Flags in a quotient lift to flags between the kernel subobject and the
whole object ([[lem-hall-flags-lift-through-a-quotient]]).

[F6] A nonzero real polynomial of degree $n$ has at most $n$ distinct real roots ([[thm-nonzero-real-polynomial-has-at-most-degree-many-distinct-roots]]).

[F7] Partition conjugation is a bijection on partitions ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

[F8] The stable symmetric-function ring is $\mathbb Z[e_1,e_2,\ldots]$,
freely generated by its elementary symmetric functions
([[def-stable-graded-ring-of-symmetric-functions]], [[thm-elementary-and-complete-families-freely-generate-the-stable-ring]]).

[F9] For each prime $p$, $\mathbb Z/p$ is a field with exactly $p$ elements
([[thm-z-mod-p-is-a-field]], [[thm-standard-representatives-modulo-n]]).

[F10] There are infinitely many primes
([[thm-euclid-infinitude-of-primes]]).

## Definition

The **Jordan quiver** has one vertex and one loop, labelled $t$:

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[>=stealth]
  \node[circle,draw,inner sep=2.5pt] (v) at (0,0) {$\bullet$};
  \draw[->] (v) edge[loop above] node {$t$} (v);
\end{tikzpicture}
```

A finite-dimensional representation over a field $k$ is a pair
$(V,x)$, where $V$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space and
$x:V\to V$ is nilpotent ([[def-nilpotent-endomorphism]]). A morphism
$(V,x)\to(V',x')$ is a linear map $f:V\to V'$ satisfying
$fx=x'f$, encoded by the commutative square

```tikzcd
V \arrow[r, "x"] \arrow[d, "f"'] & V \arrow[d, "f"] \\
V' \arrow[r, "x'"'] & V'
```

For this page, $\mathcal J_k$ denotes the small model whose objects are
$(k^n,X)$, for $n\ge0$, with $X$ a nilpotent matrix, and whose
morphisms are all matrices intertwining the endomorphisms. Every finite-
dimensional vector space is isomorphic to a standard $k^n$, so the model
represents all finite-dimensional nilpotent representations. For
$k=\mathbb F_q$, write $S=(k,0)$ for the one-dimensional object and
$I_m=(k^m,J_m(0))$ for the length-$m$ Jordan block, using
[[def-jordan-block-and-jordan-string]]. For a partition
$\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_s)$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), write
$I_\lambda$ for the block-diagonal representation with blocks
$J_{\lambda_1}(0),\ldots,J_{\lambda_s}(0)$.
Use $S^{\oplus0}=I_\varnothing=0$ for the zero object.

## Statement

Extend the generic Jordan Hall algebra of
[[thm-generic-jordan-hall-algebra-is-symmetric-functions]] to $\mathbb Q(t)$,
and use **that theorem's exact map**
$\Phi_t(u_{(1^r)})=t^{-\binom r2}e_r$.
Let $n(\lambda)$ and $b_\lambda(s)$ have the conventions of
[[def-hall-littlewood-scalar-product-and-functions]], and put
$$ a_\lambda(t)=t^{|\lambda|+2n(\lambda)}b_\lambda(t^{-1}). $$
Define the Jordan **Green pairing** to be the bilinear form
$$ (u_\lambda,u_\mu)_G=\delta_{\lambda\mu}a_\lambda(t)^{-1}. $$
It is nondegenerate and equals inverse automorphism counting at every
finite-field specialization $t=q$.
Then the Hall–Littlewood functions exist uniquely in the monic
orthogonal convention specified there, and
$$ \Phi_t(u_\lambda)=t^{-n(\lambda)}P_\lambda(x;t^{-1}),\qquad \langle P_\lambda,P_\mu\rangle_s=\delta_{\lambda\mu}b_\lambda(s)^{-1}. $$
More precisely, if $f,g\in\Lambda^d_{\mathbb Q(t)}$, then
$$ (\Phi_t^{-1}f,\Phi_t^{-1}g)_G=t^{-d}\langle f,g\rangle_{t^{-1}}. $$
Different degrees are orthogonal. In particular the transported pairing on
power sums is
$$ (\Phi_t^{-1}p_\lambda,\Phi_t^{-1}p_\mu)_G=\delta_{\lambda\mu}z_\lambda\prod_i(t^{\lambda_i}-1)^{-1}. $$
The empty partition gives $1$, with norm $1$. All the displayed basis and
pairing identities specialize at $t=q>1$ and at $s=q^{-1}$.
The pairing normalization is a degree scaling of the standard
Hall–Littlewood form; it is not the ordinary symmetric-function Hall inner
product.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The generic Jordan Hall algebra, its exact generator-normalized
map $\Phi_t$, a finite field of size $q$ for counting steps, and partitions.
All generating series below are formal: every coefficient used involves
only finite-dimensional homogeneous spaces.

[F1] The generic map is an algebra isomorphism with
$\Phi_t(u_{(1^r)})=t^{-\binom r2}e_r$; its proof establishes the Hall flag
formula and the unitriangular expansion of the monomials
$X_\lambda=\prod_j u_{(1^{\lambda'_j})}$ in Jordan classes, ordered by kernel
dimensions ([[thm-generic-jordan-hall-algebra-is-symmetric-functions]]).

[F2] The automorphism count is $a_\lambda(q)$ as displayed above
([[lem-jordan-block-automorphism-count]]).

[F3] Power sums are a basis over $\mathbb Q$ and monomial symmetric
functions are an integral stable basis
([[prop-power-sums-form-a-rational-not-integral-stable-basis]],
[[thm-monomial-symmetric-functions-form-the-integral-stable-basis]]).

[F4] Dominance compares row prefix sums, and conjugation reverses dominance
([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]], [[lem-conjugation-reverses-dominance]]).

[F5] The Hall–Littlewood form has power-sum diagonal
$z_\lambda\prod_i(1-s^{\lambda_i})^{-1}$, and its desired monic basis is
specified by orthogonality and dominance triangularity
([[def-hall-littlewood-scalar-product-and-functions]]).

[F6] Infinitely many prime cardinalities give finite fields, and a nonzero
polynomial has only finitely many real roots
([[thm-euclid-infinitude-of-primes]], [[thm-z-mod-p-is-a-field]],
[[thm-standard-representatives-modulo-n]],
[[thm-nonzero-real-polynomial-has-at-most-degree-many-distinct-roots]]).

[F7] In any commutative $\mathbb Q$-algebra $R$, the series $\exp(u)$ and
$\log(1+u)$ for $u\in zR\llbracket z\rrbracket$ are defined by their
coefficientwise finite power expansions and are inverse group homomorphisms;
in particular $\log(AB)=\log A+\log B$ for units with constant term $1$
([[def-formal-exponential-logarithm-and-powers]],
[[thm-formal-exponential-logarithm-identities]]).

## Definition

Let $k$ be a field and $n\geq 1$. The **Heisenberg Lie algebra** $\mathfrak h_n(k)$ is the $(2n+1)$-dimensional $k$-vector space with basis

$$X_1,\ldots,X_n,P_1,\ldots,P_n,Z.$$

Its bracket is the bilinear extension of

$$[P_i,X_j]=\delta_{ij}Z,\qquad [X_i,P_j]=-\delta_{ij}Z,$$

with all $[X_i,X_j]$, $[P_i,P_j]$, $[Z,X_i]$, and $[Z,P_i]$ equal to zero. Here $\delta_{ij}=1$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise. Equivalently, for coefficient vectors $a,b,a',b'\in k^n$,

$$\left[\sum_i(a_iX_i+b_iP_i)+cZ,\sum_i(a_i'X_i+b_i'P_i)+c'Z\right]=\left(\sum_i(b_i a_i'-b_i'a_i)\right)Z.$$

The Jacobi identity and alternation, including in characteristic $2$, are proved in [[lem-heisenberg-bracket-defines-lie-algebra]].

## Statement

Let $k=\mathbb F_q$, and let $I_\lambda$ denote the nilpotent Jordan-quiver
representation indexed by a partition $\lambda$, as in
[[lem-jordan-quiver-isoclasses-are-partition-indexed]]. For partitions
$\mu,\nu,\lambda$, let $g^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(q)$ be the coefficient of
$[I_\lambda]$ in the untwisted product $[I_\mu]*[I_\nu]$. There are
polynomials $G^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(t)\in\mathbb Z[t]$, independent of the
finite field, with
$$ g^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(q)=G^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(q). $$
A coefficient is zero unless $|\lambda|=|\mu|+|\nu|$.

Define the **generic Jordan-quiver Hall algebra** by
$$ H_{\mathrm{gen}}:=\bigoplus_\lambda\mathbb Z[t]u_\lambda, \qquad u_\mu*u_\nu:=\sum_\lambda G^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(t)u_\lambda, $$
giving $u_\lambda$ degree $|\lambda|$ and $t$ degree $0$.
The size condition above makes this a graded algebra.
Then $H_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is a commutative associative unital algebra and a free
polynomial algebra over $\mathbb Z[t]$ on the classes
$u_{(1^r)}$, $r\ge1$. After extending scalars to
$\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$, the assignment
$$ \Phi_t(u_{(1^r)})=t^{-r(r-1)/2}e_r $$
for every $r\ge1$, and $\Phi_t(u_\varnothing)=1$, extends uniquely to a
graded algebra isomorphism
$$ H_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_{\mathbb Z[t]}\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}] \;\cong\; \Lambda\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}], $$
where $\Lambda$ is the stable graded ring of symmetric functions.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite field $k=\mathbb F_q$, its cardinality $q$, the
Jordan-quiver category $\mathcal J_k$, and an integer $r\ge0$ when a simple
direct-sum multiplicity is used.

[F1] The untwisted product coefficient counts subobjects $N$ with quotient
$M$, and its structure constants lie in the natural numbers before their
image in a coefficient ring ([[def-untwisted-hall-algebra]]).

[F2] The product is finite-support and associative, with zero-object unit
([[lem-untwisted-hall-product-finiteness]], [[thm-untwisted-hall-algebra-is-associative-and-unital]]).

[F3] The category is finitary over every finite field

## Statement

Extend the generic Jordan Hall algebra of
[[thm-generic-jordan-hall-algebra-is-symmetric-functions]] to $\mathbb Q(t)$,
and use **that theorem's exact map**
$\Phi_t(u_{(1^r)})=t^{-\binom r2}e_r$.
Let $n(\lambda)$ and $b_\lambda(s)$ have the conventions of
[[def-hall-littlewood-scalar-product-and-functions]], and put
$$ a_\lambda(t)=t^{|\lambda|+2n(\lambda)}b_\lambda(t^{-1}). $$
Define the Jordan **Green pairing** to be the bilinear form
$$ (u_\lambda,u_\mu)_G=\delta_{\lambda\mu}a_\lambda(t)^{-1}. $$
It is nondegenerate and equals inverse automorphism counting at every
finite-field specialization $t=q$.
Then the Hall–Littlewood functions exist uniquely in the monic
orthogonal convention specified there, and
$$ \Phi_t(u_\lambda)=t^{-n(\lambda)}P_\lambda(x;t^{-1}),\qquad \langle P_\lambda,P_\mu\rangle_s=\delta_{\lambda\mu}b_\lambda(s)^{-1}. $$
More precisely, if $f,g\in\Lambda^d_{\mathbb Q(t)}$, then
$$ (\Phi_t^{-1}f,\Phi_t^{-1}g)_G=t^{-d}\langle f,g\rangle_{t^{-1}}. $$
Different degrees are orthogonal. In particular the transported pairing on
power sums is
$$ (\Phi_t^{-1}p_\lambda,\Phi_t^{-1}p_\mu)_G=\delta_{\lambda\mu}z_\lambda\prod_i(t^{\lambda_i}-1)^{-1}. $$
The empty partition gives $1$, with norm $1$. All the displayed basis and
pairing identities specialize at $t=q>1$ and at $s=q^{-1}$.
The pairing normalization is a degree scaling of the standard
Hall–Littlewood form; it is not the ordinary symmetric-function Hall inner
product.

**Given:** The generic Jordan Hall algebra, its exact generator-normalized
map $\Phi_t$, a finite field of size $q$ for counting steps, and partitions.

only finite-dimensional homogeneous spaces.

$\Phi_t(u_{(1^r)})=t^{-\binom r2}e_r$; its proof establishes the Hall flag
formula and the unitriangular expansion of the monomials
$X_\lambda=\prod_j u_{(1^{\lambda'_j})}$ in Jordan classes, ordered by kernel
dimensions ([[thm-generic-jordan-hall-algebra-is-symmetric-functions]]).

[F2] The automorphism count is $a_\lambda(q)$ as displayed above
([[lem-jordan-block-automorphism-count]]).

functions are an integral stable basis
([[prop-power-sums-form-a-rational-not-integral-stable-basis]],
[[thm-monomial-symmetric-functions-form-the-integral-stable-basis]]).

[F4] Dominance compares row prefix sums, and conjugation reverses dominance
([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]], [[lem-conjugation-reverses-dominance]]).

[F5] The Hall–Littlewood form has power-sum diagonal
$z_\lambda\prod_i(1-s^{\lambda_i})^{-1}$, and its desired monic basis is
specified by orthogonality and dominance triangularity
([[def-hall-littlewood-scalar-product-and-functions]]).

([[thm-euclid-infinitude-of-primes]], [[thm-z-mod-p-is-a-field]],

[[thm-nonzero-real-polynomial-has-at-most-degree-many-distinct-roots]]).

This page records the geometric construction and conventions for quiver
cohomological Hall algebras (CoHAs), separates the ordinary and potential
dependent constructions, and reports preprojective/Yangian actions with their
source hypotheses. The ordinary quotient-stack operation package and the standard rational vanishing-cycle realization are proved locally, followed by flag associativity.

Companion: [[cohomological-hall-algebras-and-quiver-correspondences-examples]].

## Reading prerequisites

The planned reading order is [[finitary-ringel-hall-algebras]] and
[[dg-and-homological-algebra-foundations]]. These are page-level reading
prerequisites from the plan, not item-level logical dependencies. The current
Ringel–Hall draft is count theoretic, and the current DG foundations supply
cohomological DGA/module definitions; neither supplies equivariant
Borel–Moore operations for the quiver quotient-stack correspondences.

## Scope and local results

### Untwisted CoHA

For a finite quiver $Q$ over $\mathbb C$, the page defines the
representation spaces $\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)$, their
change-of-basis quotient stacks, and the exact-sequence correspondence with
the subrepresentation first and the quotient second.
It proves the map $q$ smooth of relative stack dimension
$-\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$, and $p$ representable proper, with loops,
multiple arrows, zero coordinates, and the empty quiver included.

The untwisted product is $p_*q^!(\alpha\boxtimes\beta)$ on rational intrinsic quotient-stack homology
$\mathbb H_i([X/G])=H_{i+2\dim G}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X)$. This explicit regrading distinguishes it from the variety-normalized published equivariant Borel–Moore definition. Its convention has the subrepresentation first, no Euler-form sign twist or automorphism denominators, and no mixed-Hodge/Tate enrichment. The intrinsic homological shift is $-2\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$; conversion through the dimension of each smooth quotient stack gives the usual cohomological shift $-2\chi_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$.

The parabolic/Levi comparison uses actual induced varieties and coherent frame models. Smooth pullback across the nonrepresentable map $q$ is constructed as a vector-bundle pullback composed with the inverse of an affine-bundle pullback; proper pushforward is the incidence trace in one fixed total-dimension general linear group. The operation package proves proper/smooth base change and Cartesian pasting on the flag diagrams. Thus the two parenthesizations are the same actual three-step flag pull-push operation, and the zero representation gives the unit. These statements include all finite quivers with loops and repeated arrows. The algebraic direct sum requires no completion.

### Potential dependent and critical CoHA

A quiver potential is a cyclic class of a finite linear combination of oriented cycles. Its trace function is invariant under change of basis and additive on exact sequences. The critical construction uses rational bounded algebraically constructible vanishing cycles with positive-loop monodromy. The exact normalization is $V_f=\phi_f[-1]$, so $V_0\mathbb Q=\mathbb Q$ and the reduced $H^0$ of the $x^2$ Milnor fibre occurs in coefficient degree one.

The local Milnor-neighborhood proof supplies sector transport and the actual Thom–Sebastiani isomorphism. Principalization of the function ideal reduces the constructibility argument to a simple-normal-crossing monomial; the proper, smooth, duality and support maps are proved coherent. On an extension correspondence, Thom–Sebastiani identifies the vanishing cycles of the restricted trace function with the pullback of the diagonal coefficients. Proper functoriality gives a coefficient morphism to the total-dimension theory after duality; it does not assert a closed-restriction isomorphism.

The standard homological coefficient on $X/G$ is $K=D_X^G(V_f\mathbb Q)[-2\dim G]$. This realizes the intrinsic shift $-2\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$, retains all critical values, and gives an associative unital critical CoHA for every finite quiver with potential. For zero potential it recovers the ordinary intrinsic CoHA with the same maps and grading. The more general construction with any supplied coherent coefficient datum remains available. The algebraic direct sum needs no completion. Mixed Hodge enrichment and off-shell rapid-decay cohomology are separate theories and are not asserted by this rational realization.

### Preprojective, Nakajima, and Yangian scope

The source report distinguishes three claims: the arbitrary-finite-quiver
preprojective CoHA/action in Yang–Zhao's stated oriented-cohomology setup; the
ordinary Kac–Moody action on the Lagrangian core for quivers with no edge
loops; and the narrower Yangian comparison with its no-edge-loop condition,
sign twist, parameter specialization, torsion quotient, ADE isomorphism
range, and stated intertwining action. These are source-reported results, not
local action proofs. No general CoHA–Yangian identification is claimed.

## Definition

Let $\mathcal A$ be a small finitary abelian category in the sense of
[[def-hall-finitary-abelian-category]], and let $R$ be a commutative ring
with unit. Define the free $R$-module
$$ H_{\mathcal A,R}:=\bigoplus_{[M]\in\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal A)}R[M], $$
where $[M]$ is a basis symbol for the isomorphism class of $M$. For objects $N,L$, let
$$\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal A}(N,L):=\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(N,L): f\text{ is monic}\}.$$
This is a finite set by the Hom condition in
[[def-hall-finitary-abelian-category]]. For $f,g$ in this set, write
$f\sim_N g$ when $g=f\circ u$ for an isomorphism $u:N\to N$; this is an
equivalence relation by [[def-isomorphism-groupoid-and-connected-category]].
The quotient set $\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal A}(N,L)/\sim_N$ represents
exactly the subobjects of $L$ isomorphic to $N$: each class gives the usual
subobject class from [[def-subobject-and-quotient-object]], and the mutual-
factorisation theorem says two such monomorphisms give the same subobject
exactly when they differ by such an isomorphism
([[thm-mutual-factorisation-defines-subobject-and-quotient-object-equivalence]]).
Every subobject class with domain isomorphic to $N$ is represented by composing
its monomorphism with an isomorphism from $N$, one class at a time. The
cokernel quotient is independent of that representative by
[[thm-the-quotient-is-independent-of-the-representing-monomorphism]] and
[[def-the-quotient-of-an-object-by-a-subobject]]. Define $g^L_{M,N}$ to be the
number of classes $[f]_{\sim_N}$ for which $\operatorname{coker}(f)\cong M$.
The finiteness lemma below also proves that the resulting product has finite
support. Extend the operation
$$ [M]*[N]:=\sum_{[L]\in\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal A)}g^L_{M,N}[L] $$
$R$-bilinearly, mapping each natural number coefficient to its multiple of
$1_R$. The order is fixed: the counted short exact sequence is
$$ 0\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow0. $$

This is the **untwisted Hall product**. It does not use an Euler form, a square
root of a field size, or division by automorphism cardinalities. The finite
coefficient and finite-support claims needed for the operation to define a
bilinear product are established in
[[lem-untwisted-hall-product-finiteness]].

equivalence relation by [[def-isomorphism-groupoid-and-connected-category]].
The quotient set $\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal A}(N,L)/\sim_N$ represents
exactly the subobjects of $L$ isomorphic to $N$: each class gives the usual
subobject class from [[def-subobject-and-quotient-object]], and the mutual-
factorisation theorem says two such monomorphisms give the same subobject
exactly when they differ by such an isomorphism
([[thm-mutual-factorisation-defines-subobject-and-quotient-object-equivalence]]).
Every subobject class with domain isomorphic to $N$ is represented by composing
its monomorphism with an isomorphism from $N$, one class at a time. The
cokernel quotient is independent of that representative by
[[thm-the-quotient-is-independent-of-the-representing-monomorphism]] and
[[def-the-quotient-of-an-object-by-a-subobject]]. Define $g^L_{M,N}$ to be the
number of classes $[f]_{\sim_N}$ for which $\operatorname{coker}(f)\cong M$.
The finiteness lemma below also proves that the resulting product has finite
support. Extend the operation
$$ [M]*[N]:=\sum_{[L]\in\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal A)}g^L_{M,N}[L] $$
$R$-bilinearly, mapping each natural number coefficient to its multiple of
$1_R$. The order is fixed: the counted short exact sequence is
$$ 0\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow0. $$

This is the **untwisted Hall product**. It does not use an Euler form, a square
root of a field size, or division by automorphism cardinalities. The finite
coefficient and finite-support claims needed for the operation to define a
bilinear product are established in
[[lem-untwisted-hall-product-finiteness]].

## Statement

For a finitary abelian category, each untwisted Hall coefficient
$g^L_{M,N}$ is finite and depends only on the isomorphism classes of
$M,N,L$. For fixed $M,N$, only finitely many isomorphism classes $[L]$
have $g^L_{M,N}\ne0$. Hence the basis formula in
[[def-untwisted-hall-algebra]] is a finite sum in its direct-sum module.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finitary abelian category $\mathcal A$, objects $M,N,L$, and
the coefficient $g^L_{M,N}$ from the untwisted Hall product.

[F1] For every pair $X,Y$, the sets $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)$ and
$\operatorname{YExt}^1(X,Y)$ are finite; the latter consists of Yoneda
classes of short exact sequences with the displayed endpoints
([[def-hall-finitary-abelian-category]]).

[F2] $g^L_{M,N}$ counts equivalence classes of monomorphisms $N\to L$
under precomposition by isomorphisms of $N$, retaining those whose cokernel
is isomorphic to $M$ ([[def-untwisted-hall-algebra]]).

[F3] A morphism between short exact sequences that is the identity on both
endpoints is an isomorphism on the middle object, by the short five lemma
([[thm-short-five-lemma-in-an-abelian-category]]).

## Definition

Let $\mathcal T$ be a locally finite dg-enhancement over the finite field $\Bbbk=\mathbb F_q$ in the sense of [[def-toen-locally-finite-dg-category]]. Let $X^{(0)}$ be the core homotopy type of its perfect-module category: points are perfect modules, paths are quasi-isomorphisms, and higher paths are the derived mapping spaces. Let $X^{(1)}$ be the core homotopy type of arrows between perfect modules and $X^{(2)}$ the core homotopy type of composable pairs. These are the cores of the corresponding objectwise homotopy theories, so their equivalences are objectwise quasi-isomorphisms.

An arrow $u:x\to y$ determines three maps
$$
s(u)=x,\qquad c(u)=y,\qquad t(u)=\operatorname{Cone}(u),
$$
where $\operatorname{Cone}(u)$ is the functorial homotopy cofiber in the supplied dg enhancement. Thus $s\times t:X^{(1)}\to X^{(0)}\times X^{(0)}$ remembers the source and cofiber, and $c:X^{(1)}\to X^{(0)}$ remembers the target. For a composable pair $x\to y\to z$, write $f$ for the first arrow, $g$ for the second, $h$ for the composite, and $k:\operatorname{Cone}(f)\to\operatorname{Cone}(h)$ for the induced map of cofibers.

Set
$$
\mathcal{DH}(\mathcal T):=\mathbb Q_c(X^{(0)}).
$$
The product is the convolution
$$
\alpha*\beta:=c_!\big((s\times t)^*(\alpha\otimes\beta)\big),
$$
where $(\alpha\otimes\beta)(x,y)=\alpha(x)\beta(y)$ on $X^{(0)}\times X^{(0)}$, and $c_!$ and pullback are those of [[def-locally-finite-homotopy-type]]. For an isomorphism class $x$ of perfect modules, let $\chi_x$ be its characteristic function. The $\chi_x$ form a basis, and
$$
\chi_x*\chi_y=\sum_z g^z_{x,y}\chi_z,
$$
where $g^z_{x,y}$ is the weighted homotopy cardinality of the fiber of $c$ over $z$ restricted to arrows with source isomorphic to $x$ and cofiber isomorphic to $y$.

The zero module gives the candidate unit $\chi_0$. The definition is well-defined: local finiteness and finite support of the convolution follow from [[lem-derived-hall-moduli-spaces-and-convolution-are-finite]].

## Correspondence diagram

```tikzcd
X^{(1)} \arrow[r,"c"] \arrow[d,"s\times t"'] & X^{(0)} \\
X^{(0)}\times X^{(0)}
```

The horizontal map sends an arrow to its target; the vertical map sends it to its source and homotopy cofiber. The product pulls two input functions back along the vertical map and pushes them forward along the horizontal map. The diagram records this correspondence; it supplies no proof of associativity.

## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $H$ be a unital associative
$R$-algebra. An **$R$-linear representation of $H$** on an $R$-module $M$ is
a unital $R$-algebra homomorphism
$\rho:H\to\operatorname{End}_R(M)$, where $\operatorname{End}_R(M)$ is the
ring of $R$-linear maps $M\to M$, with composition as multiplication,
$\operatorname{id}_M$ as unit, and scalar map $r\mapsto r\operatorname{id}_M$.
It defines the unital left action
$h\cdot m:=\rho(h)(m)$; its module axioms are those of
[[def-left-and-right-modules]]. When $H$ is a Hall algebra, this structure is
called a **Hall-algebra module**.

This term does not mean an object of the input category. An input object $A$
contributes a basis symbol $[A]$ to a Hall algebra, but that symbol by itself
specifies no representation on an $R$-module. The untwisted Hall algebra
instance is supplied by
[[def-untwisted-hall-algebra]],
[[thm-untwisted-hall-algebra-is-associative-and-unital]].

The zero $R$-module is allowed; its identity endomorphism is its zero map.
This definition gives an algebra action only. An action on a tensor product
requires additional structure, such as a specified coproduct.

## Remarks

For a Green-twisted or completed Hall construction, the underlying associative
algebra and its coefficient space must first be specified; this definition
does not identify different Hall normalizations or completions.

## Definition

Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite quiver over a field $k$. A representation
of $Q$ assigns a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V_i$ to each vertex
$i\in Q_0$ and a linear map $V_{s(a)}\to V_{t(a)}$ to each arrow
$a\in Q_1$. Its dimension vector is
$\mathbf d=(\dim V_i)_{i\in Q_0}\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$.

For $\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$ put
$$\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf d}(Q) =\prod_{a\in Q_1}\operatorname{Hom}_k (k^{d_{s(a)}},k^{d_{t(a)}}),\qquad G_{\mathbf d}=\prod_{i\in Q_0}\operatorname{GL}_{d_i}(k),$$and let $\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}(Q)=[\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf d}(Q)/ G_{\mathbf d}]$ be the quotient Artin stack. It is finite type and has affine stabilizers: the representation variety and the acting group are finite type and affine, and each stabilizer is a closed subgroup of $G_{\mathbf d}$. For dimension vectors $\mathbf d,\mathbf e$, let $\mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}(Q)$ be the stack of short exact sequences of representations$$0\longrightarrow B_{\mathbf e}\longrightarrow E_{\mathbf d+\mathbf e} \longrightarrow A_{\mathbf d}\longrightarrow0.$$The endpoints are part of the data, and isomorphisms are isomorphisms of the whole exact sequence. Equivalently, after choosing the standard $\mathbf e$-dimensional subspaces at each vertex, this is the quotient by the product parabolic preserving those subspaces of the affine space of block upper-triangular arrow maps. Thus $\mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}(Q)$ is a finite-type Artin stack with affine stabilizers. More explicitly, on a local splitting $E_i=B_i\oplus A_i$, the arrow $a:i\to j$ has block matrix$$\begin{pmatrix} B_a & \xi_a\\ 0 & A_a \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \xi_a:A_i\to B_j.$$Changing the splitting by $h_i:A_i\to B_i$ changes $\xi_a$ to $\xi_a+B_a h_i-h_j A_a$. This is the translation action of the vector bundle $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,B_i)$ on $\bigoplus_{a:i\to j}\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,B_j)$ used in the extension stack calculation. Let $q:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}\to\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}$ send a sequence to its quotient, $s:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}\to \mathfrak M_{\mathbf e}$ send it to its subrepresentation, and $m:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}\to\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}$ send it to its middle representation. The Hall correspondence is ~~~ tikzcd & \mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}(Q) \ar[dl,"(q,s)"'] \ar[dr,"m"] & \\ \mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}(Q)\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf e}(Q) && \mathfrak M_{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}(Q) ~~~ Its arrows record the ordered quotient, subrepresentation, and middle object of the displayed short exact sequence; the diagram fixes the convolution convention. Define$$H_Q:=\bigoplus_{\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}} \mathscr K(\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}(Q)).$$For $\alpha\in\mathscr K(\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d})$ and $\beta\in\mathscr K(\mathfrak M_{\mathbf e})$, define$$\alpha*\beta :=m_!\big((q,s)^*(\alpha\boxtimes\beta)\big) \in\mathscr K(\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}).$$
Thus the first factor is the quotient and the second factor is the
subrepresentation, so the sequence is
$0\to B\to E\to A\to0$. Each homogeneous product is defined by one
finite-type stack correspondence; no completion or finiteness of a sum over
isomorphism classes is required. This is the stack-function product without
a potential or a vanishing-cycle weight.
